resources.string: All filled and marked cells on this puzzle will be erased. This can\'t be undone.

Fill in cells to reveal a hidden picture.

CLUES
The numbers beside each row and above each column are the lengths of the filled runs in that line, in order. "3 1" means a run of 3, at least one gap, then a run of 1. A 0 means the line is empty. Each number fades once its run is filled in exactly the right place, so they can fade in any order. When a whole row or column is right, its filled cells lock so you can't change them by accident (marks still work), and its empty cells show a dot.

TOOLS
• Fill: tap or drag to fill cells. Start on a filled cell to erase instead. A drag locks to the row or column it starts along, so it can't wander.
• Mark ✕: flag cells you know are empty. Marks are just notes.
• Pan: drag with one finger to move the zoomed board.

ZOOM
Pinch to zoom; drag with two fingers to pan. Clues stick to the edges while zoomed so you can always read them. Reset view goes back to the whole puzzle.

LIVES
Turn on lives under Options. A wrong fill or mark then costs a life and reveals the right answer for that cell. Lose them all and the puzzle starts over.

TIPS
• Start with big clues: a 7 in a 10-wide line always fills the middle 4 cells.
• Lines whose clues plus gaps add up to the full width are fully determined.
• Mark empties as you go; they make the remaining lines easier.

Progress saves automatically when you leave a puzzle. Clear wipes the board. Solved pictures appear in the Gallery, in color.
The puzzle starts over. Wrong moves reveal the right answer for that cell, so every attempt teaches you something.
Watch a one-minute tutorial that solves a small puzzle step by step. You can also find it later under Help.
This is a picross puzzle. The numbers are clues: each one is the length of a run of filled cells in that row or column, in order. Let\'s solve it together.
Row 2 says 5, and the row is only 5 wide, so every cell is filled. With Fill selected, drag along the row.
Row 3 is also a 5. Notice its clue fades: a faded number means that run is placed correctly.
Column 1 says 2, and it already has 2. The rest of it must be empty, so switch to Mark and cross those cells out. Drags skip cells that are already filled.
Same for column 5. Marks are just notes, but they make the remaining lines easier to read.
Row 4 says 3, and exactly 3 open cells are left. Fill them.
Row 1 says 1 1: two single cells with a gap between. In 3 open cells the only fit is both ends, so the middle gets a mark.
On big puzzles, pinch to zoom and drag with two fingers (or the Pan tool) to move. Clues stick to the edges so you can always read them. Reset view zooms back out.
Row 5 says 1. Column 3 needs 4 in a row and its top is marked, so its run must reach the bottom. Fill that cell to finish!
Solved! Finished pictures are revealed in color and saved to your Gallery. Your turn.
